name: Yeasted focaccia
summary: The same bread on commercial yeast — no starter, no levain build, on the table in an afternoon.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.instruction: Stir the flour, lukewarm water, yeast, salt and sugar together until no dry flour remains. No starter, no levain build — the yeast goes straight in.

steps.title: Rest, then work in the olive oil
steps.instruction: After the rest, add the olive oil and squeeze it through until the dough comes back together.

steps.title: Fold the dough
steps.instruction: When the timer goes: wet a hand, lift one side up and over into the middle, turn the bowl, repeat around.

steps.title: First rise
steps.instruction: Commercial yeast is far more predictable than a starter, so this one is close to the clock — but still look before you move on.
steps.cue: Nearly doubled and puffy, with bubbles visible at the surface.

steps.title: Oil the pan generously
steps.instruction: Pour the pan oil in and spread it up the sides. This is what crisps the base.

steps.title: Transfer the dough to the pan
steps.instruction: Tip it in gently and turn it once so it's coated in oil.

steps.title: Stretch it toward the corners
steps.instruction: Every half hour, stretch the dough gently outward by two corners. If it pulls back, leave it and come back.
steps.cue: The dough stops retracting — it stays where you put it instead of pulling back within a minute.

steps.title: Pan proof
steps.instruction: Cover and leave it somewhere warm.
steps.cue: Marshmallowy and jiggly, nearly filling the corners and sitting close to the top edge of the pan, with large bubbles under the surface.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.instruction: 230°C. If you retarded this dough in the fridge, take it out now and let it come back to room temperature — focaccia must not go into the oven cold.

steps.title: Dimple it
steps.instruction: Oil your fingers and press straight down to the bottom of the pan, about 4 cm apart.
steps.cue: Your fingertips reach the pan floor and the dough between the dimples stays puffed. If it sighs flat and doesn't recover, you pressed too hard.

steps.title: Drizzle and salt
steps.instruction: Olive oil over the surface so it pools in the dimples, then flaky salt and any toppings.

steps.title: Check it's done
steps.instruction: Lift an edge with a spatula and look underneath before you commit.
steps.cue: Brown on the raised spots, golden in the crevices, base evenly golden and crisp — not pale, not oil-logged. 88–99°C inside if you have a probe. Don't tap it for hollowness; that test doesn't work on focaccia.

steps.title: Lift it out of the pan
steps.instruction: Onto a rack straight away, or the residual oil steams the base soft.
